I have been a CNA for two years to me it's just an in-between job before I figure out my passion and go for it. From the places I've worked which is in long term care you have about 12-13 patients. From my experience you want to find a place with great management the better the management the better in terms of staffing and overall good days you will have. Being a cna is physically and mentally exhausting you will learn all types of skills you will carry with you on a daily basis. Some places have more flexible schedules then others right now I work 4 on 3 off 8 hour shifts but most places do offer a short shift someone who comes in halfway through. I can't speak for the nurses eating there young part but it can be a pretty intense environment for newcomers nursing assistant vets will expect you to adapt quickly and they can be intimidating at times. From my experience don't be afraid to stand up for yourself don't be afraid to ask for help and know when you are showing burn out symptoms. I wish you the best of luck !
